raw:
You begin with the first folder of trust-owned business papers while Nell opens the spreadsheet beside you.

The invoices are dry and orderly, clipped into yearly bundles: electrical work, film-hire charges, café supplies, a repair to the old front-door closer. You record each group by type, apparent date range, quantity, condition, and the acquisition reference Nell points out in the 2024 inventory.

“Don’t make every record a biography,” Nell says, looking over one entry. “Enough that someone can find it, understand what it is, and know why we think it belongs here.”

By mid-morning, the first box has a usable shape in the spreadsheet. A few folders have no clear date beyond a handwritten year; those go into the uncertainty notes rather than being forced into place.

Nell checks the time. “Good start. Finish this bundle, then we’ll look at the programme boxes before lunch.”
